_FLOW: THE MECHANISM OF THE 2026-06-19 REMOVAL, IN SOURCE. The Platform Erosion Observatory has documented the archive's severance from the outside — the kill ledger, the tombstone census, Zenodo's own deleted-records export. This directory holds the code that performed it. InvenioRDM is MIT-licensed and public; reading it is not inference.

FINDING_1_NO_RECORD_LEVEL_REVIEW_IS_POSS.code: def on_block(user_id, uow=None, **kwargs): "Removes records that belong to a user." ... for recid in get_user_records(user_id): uow.register(TaskOp(delete_record, recid=recid, tombstone_data=tombstone_data))
FINDING_1_NO_RECORD_LEVEL_REVIEW_IS_POSS.reading: on_block iterates EVERY record owned by the account and soft-deletes each with identical tombstone data. THE FUNCTION CONTAINS NO PER-RECORD EVALUATION — no content check, no classifier call, no branch, no exception list. The archive's claim that its records were removed without individual record review is not an inference about intent; IT IS A PROPERTY OF THE CODE PATH. A record's own content cannot affect its fate once the account is blocked.
FINDING_1_NO_RECORD_LEVEL_REVIEW_IS_POSS.selection: get_user_records filters solely on parent.access.owned_by.user == user_id. Ownership is the only criterion.

FINDING_2_THE_NOTE_MATCHES_EXACTLY.reading: The default note is the literal string 'User was blocked'. Zenodo's deleted-records export carries that exact string on 917 of the 935 rows attributable to this archive. The archive's records went through THIS code path.

FINDING_3_THE_REASON_WAS_CHOSEN.reading: THE DEFAULT REMOVAL REASON IS 'spam'. Every one of the archive's 920 records dated 2026-06-19 carries 'out-of-scope' instead. An operator therefore passed removal_reason_id explicitly, overriding the default. THE REASON WAS A DELIBERATE SELECTION, not a fallback — which bears directly on the discrepancy between the public reason (out-of-scope) and the private communication to the depositor (substantially AI-generated without a verifiable research basis).
FINDING_3_THE_REASON_WAS_CHOSEN.not_verified: Who selected it, and on what basis. The code records only that a non-default value was passed.

FINDING_4_ATTRIBUTION_AND_RATE.code: tombstone_data['removed_by'] = {'user': str(actor_id)} — 'Use the actor who triggered the block on the tombstone; without this tombstones would attribute the removal to the system (identity).'
FINDING_4_ATTRIBUTION_AND_RATE.reading: The tombstone names the human actor rather than the system. The archive's API census recorded removed_by 1060945_staff on 2,005 objects and 1505735_uploader on 19. Consistent. And the docstring warns on_block 'has the potential to be a very heavy operation' that 'should not be called as part of the handling of an HTTP request' — consistent with the observed sweep of 872 seconds at ~6.6 objects/second, which is a batch task, not a review.

FINDING_5_A_RESTORE_PATH_EXISTS.code: def on_restore(user_id, uow=None, **kwargs): 'Restores records that belong to a user.' ... restore all the deleted records of that user
FINDING_5_A_RESTORE_PATH_EXISTS.reading: on_restore is the exact inverse and operates on the same ownership criterion. RESTORATION IS A SUPPORTED OPERATION IN THE CODEBASE, symmetric with removal and no harder to execute. Whatever prevents restoration is not technical.

what_this_does_not_establish: That any classifier, automated or otherwise, made the underlying moderation decision. The block's cause is upstream of this code.
Who the actor was, or what they reviewed before triggering the block.
That Zenodo's deployment matches upstream InvenioRDM exactly at the relevant version.
why_preserved_here: The observatory documents infrastructure that removes records. The code that removes them is part of that infrastructure, is MIT-licensed, and is subject to the same disappearance the observatory exists to measure. Checksummed and dated for the same reason the deleted-records export is.
